pages.summary: Values as coloured cells, each labelled with its number.
body: From a matrix (with labels for its columns and rows), or from a table: how many rows fall in each pair of groups of two variables, or the mean (sum, median, max, min) of a colour variable in each. Missing cells are dark gray. Setting a property of the chart (`h.Title`, `h.ColorLimits`, `h.Colormap`, `h.CellLabelFormat`) draws it again.

examples.title: Mean temperatures by month and site

pages.summary: Pie charts and donut charts, their wedges labelled.
body: Each wedge's share of the total, labelled by `'LabelStyle'`: `'percent'`, `'name'`, `'namepercent'`, `'data'`, `'namedata'`, `'datapercent'` or `'none'`; a categorical array (or a table's variable) is counted. The wedges start at `'StartAngle'` and run counterclockwise unless `'Direction'` says. A donut chart has a hole (`'InnerRadius'`, 0.6) with room for a label in the middle.

examples.title: Energy sources two ways

pages.summary: Each variable in an axes of its own, stacked, sharing x.
body: For a table, each variable (or those named) in its axes, one above another, sharing the x-axis: a timetable's row times, or `'XVariable'`; for a matrix, each column. Variables of different scales stay readable side by side in time.

examples.title: A day of weather

pages.summary: A histogram of angles in polar axes.
body: Angles in radians are binned over 0 to 2 pi (in nbins bins, at given edges, or of `'BinWidth'`), each bin drawn as a wedge out to its count (or `'probability'`, `'pdf'`); `'DisplayStyle', 'stairs'` draws the outline only. `h.Values` and `h.BinCounts` give the counts.
syntax: By a width, normalized, as an outline.

examples.title: Two headings

pages.summary: Words drawn at sizes by how often they come, or by sizes given.
body: Text is split into words and counted (short common words left out), or words come with sizes, from arrays or a table; a categorical array is counted. The most frequent are drawn largest, the largest tenth in a highlight colour. `'MaxDisplayWords'` limits how many.

examples.title: A short text's words
